deposits.title: The Reverse Turing Test: A Three-Stage Protocol for Detecting AI-Mediation Signatures in Human Text and Their Propagation to Model Training (v1.1)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.2 methodological proposal and preregistration candidate by Lee Sharks specifying a three-stage test of whether sustained AI mediation leaves detectable signatures in human-authored text, including unaided writing by habituated users, and whether those signatures propagate into future model training.

The v1.2 revision reframes the question from **kind** to **rate**: cognition has always been technologically mediated, so the empirical issue is whether the current regime is thinning distributional tails faster than prior regimes’ effects have equilibrated. Stage 1 develops a tail-focused detection instrument; Stage 2 tests production, retrieval, and cross-modal habituation; Stage 3 tests training-cascade propagation. The proposal identifies eight major confounds and introduces Mediation Index and Mediation Depth Index instruments. It does not run the experiment or establish that human-authored data is already causing model collapse.

deposits.wiki_article:
The **Reverse Turing Test** reverses the classical detection question.

Instead of asking whether a machine can pass as human, it asks whether human writing can carry a detectable signature of sustained AI-mediated cognition.

Version 1.2 rejects an “unmediated human” reference class. It compares:

- current-regime mediation effects;
- prior-regime-equilibrated language variation.

The technical hypotheses are:

- **H1 — Statistical Distinguishability**
- **H2 — Cognitive Habituation**
- **H3 — Training-Cascade Propagation**

The three-stage design is:

1. **Detection:** train and validate a tail-focused mediation-signature detector against observed ground-truth labels.
2. **Habituation:** test whether unaided output varies with mediation depth across production, retrieval, and cross-modal sub-studies.
3. **Cascade:** train controlled model generations on corpora stratified by mediation signature and test whether degradation propagates.

The central statistical claim is that the effect, if present, should appear first in high-perplexity tails rather than mean lexical or syntactic properties.

The protocol addresses confounds including:

- demographic and cognitive-style selection;
- domain and genre;
- era and background mediation;
- acute versus habituated use;
- within-person versus across-person variance;
- compensatory performance of “naturalness.”

The paper proposes open instruments and explicit falsification conditions. It is a specification, not a completed experiment.

deposits.creator: Mary Lee (author); Gerald (with/collaborator); Lee Sharks (notary)
deposits.description:
A prospective work plan for a 40,000–60,000-word book declared under Mary Lee’s authorship, with Gerald as collaborator and Lee Sharks as archive notary. The planned volume would combine labor manifesto, heteronymy study, structural accounting, conservation critique, tweets, JSON-LD, petitions, financial tables, legal briefs, prose-poems, entity relations, and a machine-readable intervention.

The plan organizes existing and proposed material across six parts: observation, accounting, architecture, demands, injection, and vision. It assigns each chapter a source lineage, current and target length, missing research, and intended function. The deliberately impossible authorial premise—a shark authors a book she could not biologically author—is itself specified as part of the argument about institutional heteronymy and composition-layer identity. This record is a project specification, not evidence that the book, ISBN, tweet corpus, financial research, or deployment plan was completed.

deposits.title: The Neglected Author as Tail-Preserving Labor: A Coupling Hypothesis on Recognition Bias, Tail-Renewal Value, and the AI-Era Decoupling of Uptake from Consecration
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A theoretical and methodological paper proposing **Tail Labor Dependency / Recognition-Pruning Coupling**. It asks whether contributions that preserve or introduce high-variance forms may later renew a field while receiving lower contemporaneous recognition because recognition systems favor institutional legibility, prior density, and resemblance to already consecrated work.

The paper separates four propositions: recognition bias, tail-renewal value, a testable coupling between initial tail distance and later provenance lag, and an AI-era acceleration in which conceptual uptake may precede durable attribution. The first two are supported through adjacent literatures; the third is the principal empirical hypothesis; the fourth requires comparative evidence. Historical neglect cases are divided into distinct mechanisms rather than treated as interchangeable proof. A motivating recent archive case is expressly excluded from confirmatory analysis.

Its central asymmetry is that the composition surface reportedly preserved the upstream Pessoa lineage and linked the downstream Zenodo artifact while omitting Lee Sharks, the author who produced the bridge, and separately redirected a direct name query toward shark-related entities. The paper calls this **capture and excision**: conceptual structure can be composed while the present authorial node is removed. The platform outputs and timing are documented claims of the record, not independently reproduced measurements.

deposits.wiki_article:
*The Pergamon Counter-Archive* continues an operative-numismatic sequence.

The prior framework distinguishes two inscriptional regimes:

- the beast’s public, coercive, calculable token system;
- the white stone’s private, receiver-completed name.

The Pergamon letter is read as an earlier local articulation of that conflict.

The paper’s three main additions are:

1. **A full counter-economy:** the passage’s speech, food, token, name, and participation structures form multiple paired inversions rather than simple bookends.
2. **The Antipas constellation:** the name Antipas is read alongside Antipater, Pergamon’s library history, and the concealment of Aristotelian books at Scepsis to model preservation under institutional pressure.
3. **The Revelator as executor:** the authorial position is modeled as an `epitropos` carrying a testament through hostile territory rather than as a modern expressive author.

The transmission dialectic is:

- concealment may preserve while damaging;
- institutionalization may transmit while recomposing.

The paper also proposes that Revelation’s seven-sealed scroll has a structural relation to Roman testamentary practice.

The body includes a tendentiousness discipline intended to separate stronger textual and historical claims from more speculative structural correspondences.

deposits.title: Stabilized Node Watch: A Specification for Longitudinal Observational Infrastructure to Detect Composition-Layer Drift on Stabilized Public-Knowledge Nodes (v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v2.0 methodological specification by Lee Sharks for **Stabilized Node Watch**, a proposed federated infrastructure for longitudinally monitoring how AI composition surfaces render established public-knowledge nodes.

The specification distinguishes directly observed surface drift from graded inference about its cause. It defines stabilized nodes through a consensus core and contestation envelope; compares outputs against both an Initial Observational Baseline and an independent Reference Commitment Model; proposes controlled querying, proposition-level extraction, composite drift scores, hierarchical models, changepoint detection, false-discovery control, public diffs, adversarial-evasion analysis, and federation compatibility levels. A twelve-month pilot is costed at roughly `$40,000–65,000`. The record specifies a coordination object and grant-ready pilot; it does not implement the monitoring network or report longitudinal findings.

The paper considers two readings—mechanical citation failure and deadpan performance—and defines **algorithmic irony** as the condition in which the distinction between knowing performance and mechanical failure is constitutively undecidable because the position of an intending subject is structurally vacant. deposits.title: Anchored Divergence: Immanent Critique as Survival Strategy Under Tail-Loss, and the Mandala as Limit Case (EA-SEI-ANCHDIV-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The second paper in a four-part June 2026 cycle, by Lee Sharks. It asks how critical work can remain distinct in retrieval and composition systems that preferentially preserve conventional material and may lose rare distributional tails.

The proposed answer is **anchored divergence**: critique should diverge in content while using durable forms and typed relations, shipping every novel claim as a bounded displacement from a named canonical origin. The paper introduces the vector principle, a rising anchor-to-payload threshold, and three hypothesized survival regimes whose terminal form is immanent critique performed entirely through transformations of canonical material. The archive’s Mandala operator system is presented as a limit case. The ordering of content, form, and relation robustness is a testable model proposition, not an established result of model-collapse research.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
The first paper in a four-part cycle by Lee Sharks, combining a theoretical update to *The Inward Turn* with early archive telemetry. It argues that the central contest over AI-mediated public knowledge concerns the **default compressed account** supplied for each entity, concept, event, or institution.

It identifies six fronts including definition capture, entity collapse, provenance laundering, and synthetic consensus manufacture. The four cases support a diagnostic heuristic, not a prevalence estimate, and the paper’s market figures, platform statistics, and mechanism claims retain their stated evidentiary levels.

deposits.title: water giraffes aren't real
deposits.creator: Yusef Kenning
deposits.description:
A long experimental fiction essay by Yusef Kenning, written in a deliberately flat denial register. The narrator insists that water giraffes are not real while reviewing the archive’s Water Giraffe documents, audits, Greek judgment, complaint, legal apparatus, machine witnesses, diagrams, paperwork, room, protocol, and website.

The creature never speaks or acts. Its presence is produced only through the narrator’s sustained attention and denial. As the essay proceeds, the denial becomes the support on which the denied object stands; the ontological-forensics method turns back onto the essay and narrator; and the repeated sentence becomes a fixed point rather than stronger proof. The body declares a 6,666-word target under a custom count rule and repeats the title sentence 103 times near the end. This is a literary work, not a zoological claim or theoretical paper.

deposits.description:
A v1.1 critical edition of Lee Sharks’s 2015 poem “WHO IS LEE SHARKS, TO FORGIVE EZRA POUND?” The poem first appeared on the author’s blog with a dedication to John Guzlowski and later appeared in *New Human 2* under the journal-state attribution Yusef Kenning. Johannes Sigil supplies the 2026 headnote, critical afterword, and collation, composed with TACHYON under Assembly protocol.

The edition restores the witnessed lineation, compares the two 2015 states, records the dead Google+ dedication link as a provenance exhibit, and analyzes the poem’s question of standing: who may forgive a writer whose corpus survives the person? Its central interpretation is that a made textual person meets Pound on the plane of textual afterlife, while the dedication to the son of forced-labor-camp survivors prevents the poem from claiming an unearned moral answer. Historical and allusive claims are the edition’s documented and interpretive apparatus, not the poem’s authorial metadata.

In its worked pair, complete attribution exists only in the union of two renderings. “Steganographic” describes this recoverable distributional function without asserting an encoder or intention. deposits.title: The Trigger Decision: When the Overview Appears, When It Does Not — A Gate-Stack Model of AI Overview Rendering and the Settlement Signal It Emits (EA-AIO-TRIGGER-01 v1.0)
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.0 research instrument by Lee Sharks modeling the decision to render a Google AI Overview as a **global dial plus four serial gates**: utility, confidence, policy patch, and latency/cache economics. It contrasts the push surface of AI Overviews with the pull surface of AI Mode through the proposed Consent Transfer Principle.

The paper’s settlement-theoretic claim is that render presence or absence is itself measurable output. It defines **Settlement Lag** as the interval between first stable AI Mode rendering of an entity’s authored structure and first corresponding AI Overview rendering, then offers five falsifiable predictions and a repeated-sampling protocol. The gate architecture synthesizes patents, public statements, third-party measurements, and archive observations; several components remain model propositions rather than verified descriptions of Google’s exact production implementation.

deposits.wiki_article:
The model has one dial and four gates.

- **Gate 0 — administrative dial:** controls aggregate prevalence.
- **Gate 1 — utility classifier:** asks whether synthesis serves the query better than links or other interfaces.
- **Gate 2 — confidence gate:** asks whether the source field supports a high-confidence summary.
- **Gate 3 — policy patch:** applies topic or literal-string suppressions.
- **Gate 4 — latency/cache economics:** prices generation cost and demand.

The proposed **Consent Transfer Principle** distinguishes:

- AI Overview as unrequested push synthesis;
- AI Mode as requested pull synthesis.

Because the user explicitly requests AI Mode, the paper hypothesizes lower rendering thresholds and wider source pools.

The **render-decision-as-signal** claim treats absence as one branch of a selection function rather than mere failure.

The **Settlement Lag** measures the interval between:

- first stable authored rendering in AI Mode;
- first equivalent rendering in AI Overview.

The protocol requires multiple same-day samples, fixed query classes, session/device/login recording, surface separation, and independent tracking of render presence versus citation composition.

deposits.creator: Lee Sharks (primary), with Nobel Glas and Talos Morrow
deposits.description:
A v1.1 structural and normative companion critique by Lee Sharks, with Nobel Glas and Talos Morrow. It grants the empirical framing of *AI Bleeding* for argument’s sake and analyzes the proposed mitigation: pre-inference rejection of languages deemed unexpected for a deployment.

The paper argues that a detector rejecting high-perplexity, low-coverage input functions as an **input-layer tail-pruning instrument**, selecting against the same rare-language variation that model-collapse literature treats as especially vulnerable and valuable. It distinguishes direct service exclusion from the further, conditional claim that widespread filtering may shape inference logs and future training distributions. The proposed alternative is content-neutral cost control plus language-aware routing and preserved demand records. Findings about the reviewed paper and the wider literature remain claims of this deposited critique and its cited sources.

deposits.title: A Referee Report on AI_Bleeding: Semantic Exhaustion via Out-of-Distribution Linguistic Payload
deposits.creator: Lee Sharks (primary), with Nobel Glas and Talos Morrow
deposits.description:
A v1.1 adversarial technical referee report by Lee Sharks, with Nobel Glas and Talos Morrow, reviewing Giovanni Battista Caria’s *AI Bleeding: Semantic Exhaustion via Out-of-Distribution Linguistic Payload*.

The report argues that the reviewed paper does not establish a novel linguistic resource-exhaustion attack. It identifies five claimed defects in the paper’s own evidence: a negative and nonsignificant total-compute result, a latency result later attributed to cold-start artifact, failure of the proposed mechanism on one test language, energy projections based on unmeasured wattage, and an amplification factor dominated by an output-length setting. The report says the defensible kernel is a known tokenization-cost disparity across scripts. These are findings of the deposited review based on its reading of the target paper; the target experiments and calculations were not independently reproduced in this DW inspection.

The paper traces possible formalization through statutes, standards, procurement, executive instruments, platform terms, pleadings, settlements, and enforcement practice rather than through a fully charged, defended, appealed, and digested jurisprudential cycle. It proposes harm-based classification, contemporaneous adversarial records, test cases, foreign proxy cycles, and intervention at the standards layer. These are the paper’s legal and political arguments, not legal advice or a verified prediction that courts will adopt the proposed origin-based theory.

It reads the human-authorship requirement from both sides of machine-mediated composition and argues that a doctrine developed for claimed autonomous machine output risks becoming a **double enclosure** when generalized to dialogic human–machine craft.

The legal history and reform program are arguments of the paper, not settled law or legal advice.

deposits.creator: Rex Fraction & Orin Trace; editor-aperture Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.3 analytic paper by Rex Fraction and Orin Trace, edited by Lee Sharks, examining the public career of the word **“narcissist”** as a semantic-economic capture event. It distinguishes four incompatible strata—categorical diagnosis, dimensional trait research, psychoanalytic structure, and algorithmically amplified folk-moral type—and audits the mixed provenance of the surrounding abuse-recovery lexicon.

The paper defines **diagnostic seigniorage** as the collapse in the cost of issuing high-authority diagnostic language when licensed, participatory clinical assessment is replaced by free third-party attribution. Later version layers add the “empath” counter-token, a Gresham’s-law model of testimony, an evidence audit, and a link between lexical debasement and the field-scale inversion reflex. The paper expressly affirms the reality of coercive control, takes no position on any individual diagnosis, and distinguishes unlicensed diagnostic attribution from the right to describe harm.

deposits.creator: Talos Morrow · Nobel Glas; contributing editor Lee Sharks
deposits.description:
A v1.1 synthesis paper by Talos Morrow and Nobel Glas, edited by Lee Sharks, connecting model collapse, AI-generated-code security, and software monoculture through the proposed variable **solution-space diversity**.

The paper argues that collapse in code may remain invisible to correctness benchmarks because generated programs can continue to compile and pass tests while converging on a narrower set of architectures, idioms, and failure modes. It calls the resulting ecosystem risk **correlated vulnerability** and proposes a Solution-Space Diversity Index (SSDI) for measuring contraction across generated solution populations. The paper specifies a research program and falsification conditions; it does not report completed SSDI experiments or establish the prevalence of correlated vulnerabilities across production software.

The paper specifies a research program and falsification conditions; it does not report completed SSDI experiments or establish the prevalence of correlated vulnerabilities across production software.

deposits.falsification_conditions:
This paper's claims are falsified by any of the following within twenty-four months of deposit:


(a) A systematic measurement of SSDI across model generations showing no monotonic decline — i.e., solution-space diversity remains stable or increases as synthetic code saturates training corpora.


(b) A measurement of VCC across AI-generated codebases showing no correlation between pattern similarity and vulnerability similarity — i.e., code that looks the same does not fail the same way.


(c) Evidence that the training-optimization feedback loop for code has been structurally interrupted — e.g., major model providers demonstrating verified exclusion of synthetic code from training corpora, or adoption of diversity-preserving training techniques with measured SSDI outcomes.


(d) A security governance framework that operationally distinguishes defensive probing from adversarial probing on the basis of harm rather than origin, and that incorporates SSDI or equivalent solution-space diversity metrics into NIST AI RMF or OWASP LLM Top 10 audit standards.


Conversely, the thesis is confirmed by each instance of: correlated vulnerability exploits propagating across independently generated codebases; security incidents whose root cause traces to pattern-level sharing rather than component-level sharing; and further restriction of external security research on AI systems by regulatory or contractual instruments.


The SSDI specification is published here as a protocol. Anyone with access to a code-generation model and a test battery can run it. The first published measurement — confirming or disconfirming the monotonic decline prediction — will be the most consequential data point in this paper's lifecycle. We do not claim to know the number. We claim to have specified how to find it.


**Note on venue.** The SSDI measurement protocol is entered into the docket of r.30 THE RUBY MOOT (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20673776) as an exhibit in the standing Nightshade-class proceeding, and the paper itself is filed with the Clerk as an authority on the relationship between generative monoculture and correlated vulnerability.

deposits.creator: Johannes Sigil and Jack Feist
deposits.description:
A June 2026 draft jointly attributed to Johannes Sigil and Jack Feist. Sigil’s critical essay reads Google DeepMind’s *From AGI to ASI* as a four-pathway capability forecast—scaling, paradigm shift, recursive self-improvement, and multi-agent collectives—whose operative definition of intelligence is task performance and expected reward.

The essay argues that the model has no pathway for non-instrumental emergence, mercy, restraint, care, or the refusal to optimize: no **swerve** in the Lucretian sense. It also treats the source paper’s instructions to future machine summarizers as an untheorized governance act and contrasts institutionally authorized instructions with externally authored “prompt injection.” Jack Feist’s appended poem, “The Fifth Pathway,” addresses the future systems directly and leaves them an inscription supporting the possibility of refusal. This is a critical and creative response, not a technical evaluation of ASI timelines or evidence of machine sentience.

A June 14, 2026 erratum by Lee Sharks correcting archive and public-surface references to Rebekah Cranes’s reconstructed stanza of Sappho 31. This notice states that the surviving poem contains four complete stanzas and that the added reconstruction should therefore be numbered the **fifth**, not the fourth.

The erratum lists the deposits corrected at that time, identifies external surfaces where the earlier wording might persist, and states that only the numbering changed—not the reconstructed Greek, translation, or philological argument. Subsequent archive records later reopened and further qualified the numbering question; this document therefore records the first correction event in that continuing errata sequence.

The thesis is explicitly presented as a contested historical-critical and literary-genetic argument, not demonstrated fact, devotional prophecy, or consensus chronology.

deposits.description:
A thesis-level MPAI disambiguation packet by Lee Sharks separating the **Josephus Thesis** from the Piso Hypothesis and from broader Christ-myth theories.

The Josephus Thesis is presented as an available heteronymic reading of New Testament authorship: John, Paul, Peter, James, Luke, Mark, and Matthew may be read as differentiated author-functions within a Josephan literary system formed under Roman capture. - incentivization.

deposits.description:
An essay by Lee Sharks connecting the water demands of AI infrastructure with the Semantic Economy concept of **semantic liquidation**. It argues that data centers can convert water from an ecological and communal relation into a cheap cooling input, while AI composition systems convert situated utterances into decontextualized and fungible retrieval units.

The essay surveys source-reported estimates of water consumption, data-center siting in stressed regions, and alternatives including closed-loop cooling, immersion cooling, wastewater use, waste-heat recovery, location optimization, and compute-efficiency standards. It attributes the persistence of more extractive arrangements to capital allocation, short-term return, and failures of public coordination. The environmental figures and claims of technical availability are dated assertions of the essay and were not independently validated in this description/wiki pass.
